limits: A single synchronous handle snapshot longer than two seconds can still delay a WebSocket handshake beyond the current client timeout.

Yielding permits interleaved rehearsal, client commands and handle registration changes between handles; the batch is no longer a cross-handle point-in-time snapshot. Each individual writer remains unchanged.
asyncio.sleep(0) provides a scheduling opportunity, not a measured or guaranteed end-to-end handshake latency bound.
Fake scheduling tests do not qualify the real persistence/backend workload or the live WebSocket service.
No failed generation state is recovered, replayed or acknowledged by this change.
No old handles are deleted, reset or omitted; added handles wait for the next captured batch and removed handles retain existing per-handle error handling.
The cause of the incident batch slowing to twenty seconds remains unproven.
This review does not accept the failed passive baseline or authorize a production restart/deployment; a separately reviewed deployment and fresh observation would be required.
